title: Card Accounting Basis: the Amount Rebilled on a Dispute Resolved Against the Cardholder
content:
The amount at risk is the figure recorded as claimed on the most recent dispute standing in resolved against the cardholder status on the card account, selected by notice date. The amount rebilled on a dispute the card records as resolved against the cardholder is a computed figure rather than the whole of the temporary credit, and it never exceeds the amount at risk.

The figures that settle it on a card under Personal Credit Cards are these.

| Element | What it is |
|---|---|
| Rebilled share | 75 percent |
| Relief share on interest | 0 percent |
| Interest the relief acts on | the interest billed to the card account in the last two months added together |
| Interest relief | that interest multiplied by the relief share |
| What the share acts on | the amount at risk, with no interest relief deducted |
| Where the ceiling bites | the ceiling of the amount at risk is compared with the product |
| Rounding | the figure is rounded half-up to the cent |
| Floor | the amount rebilled is never less than 0.00 USD |

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** A card account carries one dispute recorded as resolved against the cardholder, claiming 640.00 USD, and interest charges of 22.40 USD and 19.10 USD billed in the last two months. The interest the relief acts on is 41.50 USD, and the interest relief is 0.00 USD. The rebilled share acts on 640.00 USD and gives 480.00 USD; compared with the ceiling of 640.00 USD, the lesser is 480.00 USD; rounded half-up to the cent that is 480.00 USD, which is above the floor, so 480.00 USD is rebilled.

A second card account carries two disputes recorded as resolved against the cardholder, one with a notice date in January claiming 75.00 USD and one with a notice date in May claiming 210.33 USD. The May dispute is the most recent by notice date, so the amount at risk is 210.33 USD; the product is 157.7475, which rounds half-up to the cent as 157.75 USD.
